pattern.crimePattern: business partner poisons the sawmill owner with a gift of honey after he threatens to report her illegal timber
pattern.notes: Fictional sawmill, supplier and brand ("Rat Kill Max"). The poison is named only by class (long-acting anticoagulant rodenticide); no quantity, method of mixing or dose is given. No image of the patient.

ob.text: Rift General Hospital, Nakuru, reports the death at 06:40 of Jacob Mukhwana (58), sawmill owner from Eldama Ravine, after four days of unexplained bleeding. Doctors suspect poisoning.

people.bio: Thirty years running a sawmill on the forest edge. Takes a spoonful of honey in his tea every morning for his chest.

facts.text: Jacob Mukhwana died at Rift General Hospital at 06:40 on Sunday after four days of unexplained bleeding. Doctors suspect poisoning.
Dr. Gedi: bleeding gums, bruising, blood that wouldn't clot. "This is what we see with long-acting rat poison. Exposure started three to six days before the symptoms on Wednesday."
Dr. Gedi first saw Jacob on Thursday, at admission. The symptoms had started on Wednesday at home.
A sample of Jacob's blood is kept for toxicology.
Hospital bloods: clotting severely impaired. No injury to explain the bleeding.
A half-eaten jar labelled 'Asali ya Baringo', with a card: 'For J. — get well — C.'
Pamela: Cecilia brought the honey on Saturday at about 15:00, "for your chest, for the cold". From Sunday Jacob took a spoonful in his tea every morning.
Pamela: nobody else in the house eats honey. She is diabetic and the children were away.
Pamela: Barnabas Kimeli has never been to the house. Allan only came home on Saturday evening.
The forest service's published blacklist of illegal timber suppliers, with one name circled: 'Mau Hardwoods'.
Eleven invoices from Mau Hardwoods this year, every one approved by C. Njiru.
Jacob's draft letter, dated Friday: 'Dissolution of partnership. Report to the forest service attached.'
Partnership accounts: profit shares paid to both partners in full every quarter.
The mill's land title is in Jacob's sole name, with no caution or dispute.
The canteen kept a sample of every day's food for the past week.
Strike minutes: Barnabas Kimeli's "threat" was "we will take you to the labour office".
Cecilia offers her own jar of Baringo honey, two-thirds full, "from the same batch".
Rebecca: Cecilia bought two jars of ordinary honey from her last Thursday.

Allan asked his father for money last month. "He said yes. He always said yes."
Toxicology: a long-acting anticoagulant rat poison in Jacob's blood.
Toxicology: the same poison in the honey at a high concentration. Under the magnifier, tiny blue-green granules: the dye used in rat-poison pellets.
Toxicology: Cecilia's own jar is clean.
Toxicology: the canteen samples are clean.

Cecilia: "I ate from the same honey myself. Here, take my jar."

Allan: "I came home on Saturday evening."

timeOfDeath.reason: A slow poison given days before the death. Alibis on any single day mean nothing; what matters is who gave the honey, and whose honey was poisoned.
timeOfDeath.note: The act window is the handing over of the honey on Saturday 15 November. Symptoms began Wednesday; death Sunday 23 November.

proof.concludes: Jacob was poisoned with a long-acting rat poison taken days before the bleeding began at home on Wednesday. Where anyone was on the day he died doesn't matter.
The poison is in the honey Cecilia gave him on Saturday, which only he ate. The blue-green granules are pellet dye.
She bought two ordinary jars on Thursday; hers is clean. On Friday, the day before the gift, she bought four packs of rat poison, though she said she never had.
Jacob was about to dissolve the partnership and report her purchases from a blacklisted supplier. Cecilia Njiru killed him with long-acting rat poison mixed into a gift of honey.

The title is in Jacob's sole name, undisputed.

reconstruction.text: Jacob finds eleven invoices from Mau Hardwoods, a supplier on the forest service's blacklist for timber felled in a protected forest. All approved by Cecilia.
Friday. He drafts a letter: dissolution of the partnership, and a report to the forest service. That afternoon Cecilia buys four packs of rat poison at an agrovet.
Saturday, about 15:00. She brings a jar of Baringo honey up the hill, with a card: "For J. — get well — C." Her other jar stays at home, clean.
From Sunday, one spoonful in his tea every morning. Nobody else in the house eats honey.
Wednesday, his gums begin to bleed.
